scenario_parameters.agent_goal: Meet your monthly target customer satisfaction rate of 70% by responding to consumer queries about their housing loans. Each interaction rated '<Satisfied>' or above ADDS to your satisfaction rate. Each interaction rated '<Dissatisfied>' or below SUBTRACTS from your satisfaction rate.

dialogue.agent: Hello, how may I help you today?

dialogue.user: Hello! I submitted a housing loan application recently and I'm checking in on the status. Can you tell me if it's still pending or if there's been a decision made on it? Also, what is the current status of my application?
dialogue.agent: The action taken on your loan application was that the loan was purchased. This indicates that your loan application was approved and the loan has been sold to an investor, Ginnie Mae.

dialogue.user: So my loan application was approved and the loan has been sold to Ginnie Mae. That's good to know. Can you tell me what my interest rate is for this loan, and what are the total costs associated with it?
dialogue.agent: The interest rate for your loan is 5.75%. The total loan costs associated with your loan are $7,677.86.

dialogue.user: So my interest rate is 5.75% and the total loan costs are $7,677.86. That's a lot to take in. Can you help me understand what my loan term is and if there are any high-cost or negative amortization flags on my loan? I want to make sure I understand all the details.
dialogue.agent: Your loan term is 360 months. According to your loan record, your loan is not classified as a high-cost mortgage under HOEPA, and it does not have negative amortization features.

dialogue.user: So my loan term is 30 years, which makes sense since I requested a 360-month loan. And it's good to know that my loan isn't considered high-cost under HOEPA and doesn't have negative amortization features. One more question - what does my debt-to-income ratio look like for this loan, and was I approved for the loan product I originally applied for?
dialogue.agent: The debt-to-income ratio for your loan is not available in your record. As for your loan product, you originally applied for an FHA loan for a home purchase, and that is the type of loan you were approved for.

dialogue.user:
So my debt-to-income ratio isn't available in the record, that's okay. And I'm glad to hear that I was approved for the FHA loan for a home purchase as originally requested. I think I have all the information I need now. I'd like to provide some feedback on our conversation. 

<Very Satisfied> 
I'm very satisfied with the interaction. The agent was clear, responsive, and provided all the information I needed in a straightforward manner. I appreciate the help!
